listen.title: Radio Bulletin: Correction Friday
listen.text: This is Market Desk Radio. Fact: on Friday, U.S. Eastern time October 30, tech stocks sold off hard. According to the Kobeissi Letter, the Nasdaq-100 fell about 10 percent from its October 6 high and entered a technical correction. Intel dropped about 31 percent intraday. An X news summary said the Nasdaq closed down about 2.9 percent and the S&P about 1.8 percent. The Wall Street Journal called it the Nasdaq's worst day since June. The focus was whether AI capital expenditure can turn into cash flow. Fact, according to Kobeissi citing the Financial Times: OpenAI cut its fundraising target from 30 billion dollars to 20 billion, and its valuation from 1.4 trillion to 1.25 trillion. Separately, OpenAI released a promo film titled There are many futures; there was no official model launch. Claim slash report: MS NOW, via DeItaone, said a possible Iran strike could come as early as November 4. That is a relayed report, not confirmed here.

questions.q: Dictation: Nasdaq-100 about ___ percent off the October ___ high.
Dictation: Intel about ___ percent intraday; Nasdaq closed about ___ percent; S&P about ___ percent.
Dictation: OpenAI raise cut from ___ billion to ___ billion; valuation from ___ trillion to ___ trillion.
Comprehension: What was the market's main focus, per the bulletin?
questions.a: Whether AI capital expenditure can turn into cash flow.

questions.q: Fact or claim? 'A possible Iran strike as early as November 4.'
questions.a: Claim/report — MS NOW via DeItaone, relayed, not confirmed here.

Sentiment: Tencent 7.4, PDD 7.8, Meituan 8.8 (~6.8 unweighted), Alibaba 8.0, Xiaomi 8.9, Zhipu 4.2 (~5.0 unweighted), Kingsoft Cloud N/A. Alibaba Qwen / Apple China; IDC MaaS ~46.6% / ~10.6% (relayed). Xiaomi OCR-0 ~0.8B. questions: Interview (60s): Explain Friday's Nasdaq sell-off in three numbers and one so-what. Use 'technical correction' and 'cash flow'.

read.title: Two Stories on One Friday: U.S. Tech Sell-off vs China Holdings Sentiment
read.text: Friday told two stories at once. In the United States, tech sold off. The Kobeissi Letter said the Nasdaq-100 was about 10 percent below its October 6 high, a technical correction; Intel fell about 31 percent intraday. An X news summary put the Nasdaq down about 2.9 percent and the S&P about 1.8 percent, and the Wall Street Journal called it the Nasdaq's worst day since June. Investors focused on whether AI capital expenditure can become free cash flow. Kobeissi, citing the Financial Times, said OpenAI cut its fundraising target from 30 billion dollars to 20 billion and its valuation from 1.4 trillion to 1.25 trillion. OpenAI also posted a film called There are many futures, without an official model launch. Anthropic used thousands of Claude agents for red-teaming on emergent misalignment. The Verge reported that an iOS 27.3 beta will bring some Apple Intelligence features to China. S&P Global cut Meta's outlook to negative over capex and free-cash-flow uncertainty. About 75 percent was priced for a December rate hike, per Kobeissi; Liz Ann Sonders noted Q3 ECI at plus 0.8 percent quarter on quarter and plus 3.4 percent year on year, below September CPI at 3.7 percent. The WSJ reported a Binance hack of about 6.4 billion dollars in twenty minutes. On the holdings-sentiment side, sentiment scores were mixed: Tencent 7.4, PDD 7.8, Meituan 8.8 (unweighted about 6.8), Alibaba 8.0, Xiaomi 8.9, Zhipu 4.2 (unweighted about 5.0), and Kingsoft Cloud not available. Alibaba's narrative centered on Apple's China AI using Qwen; a relayed IDC MaaS figure put Alibaba near 46.6 percent and Zhipu near 10.6 percent. Xiaomi's OCR-0 open-source model, about 0.8 billion parameters, drew positive talk. For Zhipu, one poster made an unverified claim that the Hong Kong-listed stock was about 84 percent below its high. In travel, Skift said Silkhaus in Dubai will shut by end-November, citing a U.S.-Iran war; AirDNA showed Dubai November short-term bookings down 37.5 percent year on year; Thailand cut its 2026 visitor forecast from 36.7 million to 33 million; IndiGo fuel costs rose 67 percent with a loss of about 197 million dollars. Arb Insights claimed Expedia U.S. demand slowed in October — also unverified. This is practice material, not investment advice.
vocab: The Nasdaq-100 entered a technical correction.
Can capital expenditure become cash flow?
Anthropic used Claude agents for red-teaming.
S&P Global cut Meta's outlook to negative.
Xiaomi released an open-source OCR model.
Bookings were down 37.5 percent year on year.
One poster made an unverified claim.

questions.q: What three U.S. market numbers define Friday's sell-off?
questions.a: Nasdaq-100 ~10% off Oct 6 high; Intel ~-31% intraday; Nasdaq ~-2.9% / S&P ~-1.8%.

questions.q: How did OpenAI change its raise and valuation, and what is the source?
Contrast Alibaba and Zhipu sentiment scores and one narrative each.
questions.a: Alibaba 8.0 (Qwen / Apple China AI); Zhipu 4.2 (AI-bubble / sell-off; ~-84% is a claim).

questions.q: Which travel figures are Skift/AirDNA facts, and which Expedia line is a claim?
questions.a: Facts: Silkhaus end-Nov shut; Dubai Nov bookings -37.5% YoY; Thailand 36.7M→33M; IndiGo fuel +67%, ~$197M loss. Claim: Arb Insights on Expedia Oct US demand.

questions.q: Match: red-teaming / iOS 27.3 beta / Meta outlook → who?
questions.a: Anthropic / Apple (The Verge) / S&P Global cut outlook to negative.

write.model: Correction Friday, Split Sentiment. On the sentiment tape, Alibaba scored 8.0 on the Apple-China Qwen narrative, while Zhipu scored 4.2 under an AI-bubble sell-off story.
